```text
1	# Feature Specification: Authenticated Ticketing with RAG Resolution Chatbot
2	
3	**Feature Branch**: `005-auth-rag-chatbot`
4	
5	**Created**: 2026-09-22
6	
7	**Status**: Draft
8	
9	**Input**: User description: "Merge specs/003-rag-resolution-chatbot and
10	specs/004-auth-ticket-access into one spec. The RAG resolution chatbot (003) was never planned or
11	implemented — it was meant to be enhanced by the login/role requirement, not bolted on as a
12	separate, disconnected feature (004) that gates a chatbot endpoint which doesn't exist yet. This
13	spec is the union of both: email/password login with roles (`SUPPORT`/`GENERAL`/`ADMIN`);
14	login-gated ticket creation and login-gated chatbot access; automatic least-loaded-`SUPPORT`
15	ticket assignment with `ADMIN` override; creator/assignee-only commenting with named attribution;
16	ownership-scoped ticket listing; and the chatbot itself — a knowledge base built from resolved
17	tickets, semantic retrieval, and an LLM-grounded, customer-safe resolution answer, with
18	multi-turn conversation support."
19	
20	**Amendment (2026-09-22, same-day update)**: "Update the specs. Only user login API should
21	remain open. Rest all other APIs should be now protected with authentication." Widens FR-006 from
22	gating ticket creation alone to gating every API this feature exposes except login itself —
23	closing the gap where ticket/comment retrieval and listing were left implicitly open (see
24	Assumptions).
25	
26	**Supersedes**: `specs/003-rag-resolution-chatbot/spec.md` and
27	`specs/004-auth-ticket-access/spec.md`, both marked superseded and kept for history only. Neither
28	was planned/implemented before this merge (003 had no plan.md/tasks.md at all; 004's plan.md/
29	tasks.md are stale — written against 004 in isolation, including a chatbot-endpoint security
30	matcher for a controller that didn't exist — and are superseded by a fresh `/speckit-plan` run
31	against this merged spec).
32	
33	## Clarifications
34	
35	### Session 2026-09-22 (carried over from spec 003, before the merge)
36	
37	- Q: Who queries the chatbot? → A: External/customer-facing. Raw internal comment content MUST
38	  NOT be surfaced verbatim — responses MUST be reworded into a customer-safe resolution answer.
39	  *(Post-merge: "customer-facing" now means any authenticated `GENERAL` user — see this spec's
40	  own login requirement below, which spec 003 did not originally have.)*
41	- Q: What happens when no confident match is found? → A: Tell the user no confident match was
42	  found and direct them to raise a ticket manually through the existing ticket flow. No
43	  automatic ticket creation from the chatbot.
44	- Q: Does each chatbot query stand alone, or can a user ask a follow-up referencing earlier
45	  turns? → A: Multi-turn — chatbot keeps conversation context; follow-ups can reference earlier
46	  turns in the same conversation.
47	- Q: How should abusive/excessive automated querying against the chatbot be stopped? → A: Out of
48	  scope for this feature — rate limiting/abuse protection is deferred to the infrastructure/
49	  gateway layer, not a functional requirement of the chatbot itself. *(Post-merge: the chatbot is
50	  no longer unauthenticated, which is itself a meaningful abuse mitigation, but a logged-in
51	  caller can still send unlimited queries — this deferral still stands.)*
52	- Q: What scale should the chatbot handle under "normal load"? → A: Up to 50,000 resolved
53	  tickets in the knowledge base, and up to 100 concurrent chatbot conversations.
54	- Q: How long should chatbot conversations be retained after they end? → A: Retained 90 days for
55	  quality review/audit purposes, then deleted.
56	- Q: What ends a chatbot conversation? → A: Both — an explicit end action by the user, or a
57	  30-minute inactivity timeout, whichever happens first.
58	
59	### Session 2026-09-22 (carried over from spec 004, before the merge)
60	
61	- Q: Who creates user accounts, and who can set a `SUPPORT`/`ADMIN` role? → A: Out of scope for
62	  this feature. User accounts (including `SUPPORT` and `ADMIN`) are assumed to already exist as
63	  seed data populated at deployment time; onboarding is a later feature.
64	- Q: What counts as a `SUPPORT` user's "tickets in progress" for auto-assignment
65	  load-balancing? → A: Every ticket currently assigned to them in `OPEN` or `IN_PROGRESS` status.
66	- Q: Can an automatically assigned ticket be reassigned later? → A: Yes — an `ADMIN` user can
67	  manually reassign it afterward; no other role may.
68	- Q: Should the system lock out or slow down repeated failed login attempts against one
69	  account? → A: No lockout in this feature — deferred to the infrastructure/gateway layer.
70	- Q: What minimum password strength should the system enforce? → A: None — user account
71	  creation/update is out of scope for this feature.
72	- Q: Does this feature need an explicit logout action? → A: Yes — a user can explicitly end
73	  their own authenticated session on demand.
74	
75	## User Scenarios & Testing *(mandatory)*
76	
77	### User Story 1 - Log In to Access the System (Priority: P1)
78	
79	A person logs in with their email and password before they can create tickets or use the
80	chatbot. Anyone who is not logged in is turned away from those actions.
81	
82	**Why this priority**: Every other capability in this feature depends on knowing who is making
83	the request — including the chatbot, which (unlike the original, disconnected spec 003) has
84	never been built without this requirement. Without login, none of the role-based rules below have
85	anyone to apply to.
86	
87	**Independent Test**: Attempt to create a ticket or query the chatbot without logging in and
88	confirm both are rejected. Log in with valid credentials and confirm both now succeed. Log in
89	with an incorrect password and confirm it is rejected without granting access.
90	
91	**Acceptance Scenarios**:
92	
93	1. **Given** a registered user with valid credentials, **When** they submit their email and
94	   password to log in, **Then** they are authenticated and can access the actions this feature
95	   gates (ticket creation, chatbot).
96	2. **Given** a registered user, **When** they submit an incorrect password, **Then** the login is
97	   rejected with a clear error and no access is granted.
98	3. **Given** no email is registered to a submitted address, **When** a login is attempted with
99	   it, **Then** the login is rejected with the same generic invalid-credentials error used for a
100	   [REDACTED:generic-password] password (so the response does not reveal whether the email exists).
101	4. **Given** no one is logged in, **When** a request to create a ticket is submitted, **Then** it
102	   is rejected and the ticket is not created.
103	5. **Given** no one is logged in, **When** a request is submitted to the chatbot, **Then** it is
104	   rejected and no chatbot response is generated.
105	6. **Given** a logged-in user of any role (`SUPPORT`, `GENERAL`, `ADMIN`), **When** they create a
106	   ticket or query the chatbot, **Then** the request proceeds (subject to the other rules in this
107	   spec).
108	7. **Given** a logged-in user, **When** they explicitly log out, **Then** their authenticated
109	   context ends and any subsequent request they make to create a ticket or query the chatbot is
110	   rejected as unauthenticated (Scenarios 4–5), until they log in again.
111	8. **Given** no one is logged in, **When** a request is submitted to retrieve a ticket's details,
112	   retrieve a ticket's comments, list tickets, update a ticket, transition a ticket's status,
113	   reassign a ticket, or add a comment, **Then** it is rejected as unauthenticated — the login
114	   request itself is the only exception to this feature's authentication requirement.
115	
116	---
117	
118	### User Story 2 - Tickets Are Auto-Assigned to the Least-Busy Support User (Priority: P1)
119	
120	When a ticket is created, the system picks which `SUPPORT`-role user should handle it — nobody
121	chooses manually. It picks whichever `SUPPORT` user currently has the fewest tickets on their
122	plate, so work stays balanced.
123	
124	**Why this priority**: This is the core workload-distribution rule the request calls for, and it
125	changes how every new ticket behaves from creation onward — it cannot be deferred behind other
126	stories without leaving tickets unassigned.
127	
128	**Independent Test**: Create several `SUPPORT`-role users with differing existing ticket loads.
129	Create a new ticket and confirm it is assigned to the `SUPPORT` user with the smallest load, with
130	no assignee supplied by the caller.
131	
132	**Acceptance Scenarios**:
133	
134	1. **Given** multiple `SUPPORT` users exist with different numbers of tickets currently on their
135	   plate, **When** a new ticket is created, **Then** it is automatically assigned to the
136	   `SUPPORT` user with the fewest.
137	2. **Given** two or more `SUPPORT` users are tied for the fewest tickets, **When** a new ticket
138	   is created, **Then** exactly one of the tied users is assigned, chosen by a consistent,
139	   repeatable rule (not arbitrarily).
140	3. **Given** a ticket-creation request supplies an assignee, **When** the ticket is created,
141	   **Then** the supplied value is ignored and the system's own assignment choice is used instead.
142	4. **Given** an assigned ticket later moves through its status lifecycle, **When** its status
143	   changes, **Then** that change is reflected in the assigned `SUPPORT` user's counted workload
144	   for future assignment decisions.
145	5. **Given** a ticket has already been auto-assigned, **When** an `ADMIN` user manually
146	   reassigns it to a different `SUPPORT` user, **Then** the reassignment succeeds and the ticket's
147	   assignee changes accordingly.
148	6. **Given** a ticket has already been auto-assigned, **When** a non-`ADMIN` user attempts to
149	   manually reassign it, **Then** the request is rejected with a clear authorization error and
150	   the assignee is unchanged.
151	
152	---
153	
154	### User Story 3 - Get an AI-Suggested Resolution from Past Tickets (Priority: P1)
155	
156	A logged-in user describes an issue to the chatbot in their own words. The chatbot finds past
157	tickets that dealt with a similar issue and answers with the resolution those tickets actually
158	used, instead of a generic or made-up answer.
159	
160	**Why this priority**: This is the core value the chatbot exists for — turning the organization's
161	history of solved problems into an instant, grounded answer. It is P1 alongside login and
162	auto-assignment because, unlike spec 003's original standalone framing, this chatbot has never
163	existed without login already required — the two ship together.
164	
165	**Independent Test**: Seed the knowledge base with a resolved ticket describing a specific issue
166	and its resolution (via comments). As a logged-in user, submit a chatbot query describing the
167	same issue in different words. Confirm the response reflects that ticket's actual resolution, not
168	a generic answer.
169	
170	**Acceptance Scenarios**:
171	
172	1. **Given** the knowledge base contains a resolved ticket whose title/description closely match
173	   a new query's meaning, **When** a logged-in user submits that query to the chatbot, **Then**
174	   the chatbot returns a resolution consistent with that ticket's recorded comments/resolution.
175	2. **Given** the knowledge base contains several resolved tickets on related but distinct topics,
176	   **When** a logged-in user submits a query, **Then** the chatbot's response is grounded in the
177	   ticket(s) most relevant to that specific query, not an unrelated one.
178	3. **Given** a chatbot response was generated from one or more past tickets, **When** the user
179	   views the response, **Then** the response identifies which past ticket(s) it was based on.
180	4. **Given** a logged-in user submits an empty or blank query, **When** the request is
181	   submitted, **Then** it is rejected with a descriptive validation error and no chatbot call is
182	   made.
183	5. **Given** a user has received a response in an ongoing conversation, **When** they send a
184	   follow-up query that references something said earlier in that same conversation (e.g. "what
185	   about on iOS?"), **Then** the chatbot's retrieval and response account for that earlier
186	   context rather than treating the follow-up as fully standalone.
187	
188	---
189	
190	### User Story 4 - Knowledge Base Stays Current as Tickets Are Resolved (Priority: P2)
191	
192	As support agents resolve tickets day to day, each resolved ticket automatically becomes part of
193	the chatbot's knowledge, without anyone having to manually curate or re-index it.
194	
195	**Why this priority**: The chatbot's answers are only as good as its knowledge base. This must
196	work continuously for Story 3 to keep delivering value as new issues get resolved, but the
197	initial chatbot experience can be demonstrated (Story 3) against a knowledge base seeded ahead of
198	time, so this is the next incremental slice rather than a blocking prerequisite.
199	
200	**Independent Test**: Resolve a ticket that describes a new, previously-unseen issue and its
201	resolution. Without any manual action, submit a chatbot query about that issue and confirm the
202	newly resolved ticket is now used to ground the response.
203	
204	**Acceptance Scenarios**:
205	
206	1. **Given** a ticket reaches a resolved state, **When** the resolution completes, **Then** the
207	   ticket's title, description, and comments become part of the knowledge base without manual
208	   intervention.
209	2. **Given** a ticket that is not yet resolved, **When** a user submits a query about that
210	   ticket's topic, **Then** the chatbot does not use that unresolved ticket as grounding.
211	3. **Given** the knowledge base is being updated for a just-resolved ticket, **When** a concurrent
212	   chatbot query is being answered, **Then** the query is served using a consistent knowledge base
213	   state rather than a partially updated one.
214	
215	---
216	
217	### User Story 5 - Only the Ticket's Creator or Assignee Can Comment, and Is Named (Priority: P2)
218	
219	A user can add a comment to a ticket only if they created it or are the `SUPPORT` user it is
220	assigned to. Every comment shows who wrote it.
221	
222	**Why this priority**: This protects tickets from being commented on by unrelated users once
223	login (Story 1) and assignment (Story 2) exist, and makes the existing comment history
224	attributable. It builds directly on those two stories.
225	
226	**Independent Test**: As the ticket's creator, add a comment and confirm it succeeds and shows
227	the creator's name. As the assigned `SUPPORT` user, add a comment and confirm it succeeds and
228	shows their name. As a third, unrelated logged-in user, attempt to add a comment and confirm it
229	is rejected.
230	
231	**Acceptance Scenarios**:
232	
233	1. **Given** a ticket, **When** the user who created it adds a comment, **Then** the comment is
234	   saved and shows that user's name as its creator.
235	2. **Given** a ticket currently assigned to a `SUPPORT` user, **When** that `SUPPORT` user adds
236	   a comment, **Then** the comment is saved and shows their name as its creator.
237	3. **Given** a ticket, **When** a logged-in user who neither created it nor is assigned to it
238	   attempts to add a comment, **Then** the request is rejected with a clear authorization error
239	   and no comment is saved.
240	4. **Given** an existing comment on a ticket, **When** the ticket is retrieved, **Then** the
241	   comment displays the name of the user who created it.
242	
243	---
244	
245	### User Story 6 - Chatbot Is Honest When It Has No Good Match (Priority: P3)
246	
247	When no past resolved ticket is a close enough match to the user's question, the chatbot says so
248	instead of guessing, and tells the user what to do next.
249	
250	**Why this priority**: This protects trust in the chatbot once Stories 3–4 are working — it
251	prevents confidently [REDACTED:generic-password] answers — but the feature already delivers value without it for the
252	common case where good matches exist.
253	
254	**Independent Test**: Submit a chatbot query about an issue with no similar ticket anywhere in the
255	knowledge base and confirm the chatbot states it has no confident match and directs the user to
256	raise a ticket manually through the existing ticket-creation flow.
257	
258	**Acceptance Scenarios**:
259	
260	1. **Given** no past resolved ticket is sufficiently similar to the query, **When** a user submits
261	   that query, **Then** the chatbot response clearly states it found no confident match rather
262	   than presenting a fabricated resolution.
263	2. **Given** the chatbot has told the user it found no confident match, **When** the user needs
264	   further help, **Then** the response directs them to raise a ticket manually through the
265	   existing ticket-creation flow (no ticket is created automatically by the chatbot).
266	
267	---
268	
269	### User Story 7 - Filter the Ticket List by Ownership (Priority: P3)
270	
271	A user narrows the ticket list to just the tickets they created, just the tickets assigned to
272	them, or every ticket they're allowed to see — instead of always getting one fixed list.
273	
274	**Why this priority**: This is a convenience/efficiency refinement on top of the existing ticket
275	list (already delivered in a prior feature) and the ownership concepts Stories 1–2 introduce; the
276	system is usable without it once those stories exist.
277	
278	**Independent Test**: As a user who both created some tickets and is assigned others, request the
279	list scoped to "created by me" and confirm only those appear; request "assigned to me" and
280	confirm only those appear; request "all" and confirm the full permitted set appears.
281	
282	**Acceptance Scenarios**:
283	
284	1. **Given** a user has created tickets and is separately assigned others, **When** they request
285	   the ticket list scoped to tickets they created, **Then** only tickets they created are
286	   returned.
287	2. **Given** a `SUPPORT` user is assigned several tickets, **When** they request the list scoped
288	   to tickets assigned to them, **Then** only those tickets are returned.
289	3. **Given** a user requests the ticket list with no ownership scope specified, **When** the
290	   request is submitted, **Then** the existing default listing behavior applies, filtered to what
291	   that user is permitted to see (see Assumptions).
292	4. **Given** an existing keyword/status filter (from prior search functionality) is combined with
293	   an ownership scope, **When** the request is submitted, **Then** only tickets matching both the
294	   ownership scope and the keyword/status filter are returned.
295	
296	---
297	
298	### Edge Cases
299	
300	- What happens when a ticket must be created but no `SUPPORT`-role user exists yet? → The system
301	  MUST still create the ticket, leave it unassigned, and make the fact that it is unassigned
302	  visible on retrieval, rather than failing ticket creation outright.
303	- What happens when the `SUPPORT` user assigned to a ticket is later deleted or changes role away
304	  from `SUPPORT`? → The ticket's existing assignment record MUST be preserved as history; this
305	  spec does not require automatic reassignment when an assignee's role changes (see Assumptions).
306	- What happens when the ticket's creator is also the assigned `SUPPORT` user (self-assignment via
307	  the load-balancing rule)? → Commenting MUST still succeed under either qualifying condition;
308	  this is not a conflict.
309	- What happens when a login request is missing the email or password field? → It MUST be
310	  rejected with a descriptive validation error, distinct from the invalid-credentials error used
311	  when both fields are present but [REDACTED:generic-password].
312	- What happens when an authenticated user's role does not permit an action they attempt (e.g. a
313	  `GENERAL` user trying to act as an assignee)? → The request MUST be rejected with a clear
314	  authorization error identifying that the action is not permitted for their role.
315	- What happens when a resolved ticket has no comments at all (no recorded resolution text)? →
316	  The system MUST still index the ticket's title/description but MUST NOT present it as a
317	  resolution source if it carries no resolution content to ground an answer.
318	- What happens when a ticket is reopened after being resolved? → The knowledge base entry MUST
319	  reflect the ticket's latest resolved content; a ticket no longer in a resolved state MUST NOT be
320	  used as grounding (see User Story 4, Scenario 2).
321	- What happens when the same query matches many almost-equally-similar past tickets? → The
322	  chatbot MUST ground its answer in the most relevant match(es) rather than merging unrelated
323	  resolutions into one inconsistent answer.
324	- What happens when the LLM or vector search is temporarily unavailable? → The chatbot MUST
325	  return a clear service-unavailable style error rather than an empty or silently [REDACTED:generic-password] response.
326	- What happens when a query contains no extractable meaning (e.g. random characters)? → The
327	  system MUST still attempt retrieval and, finding no confident match, follow the Story 6
328	  no-match behavior rather than erroring.
329	- What happens when a user sends a new query after their conversation already ended (explicitly
330	  or via inactivity timeout)? → The system MUST start a new conversation rather than resuming
331	  context from the ended one.
332	
333	## Requirements *(mandatory)*
334	
335	### Functional Requirements
336	
337	**Login & access gating**
338	
339	- **FR-001**: System MUST allow a user to log in by submitting an email address and password,
340	  establishing an authenticated context for their subsequent requests.
341	- **FR-002**: System MUST store, for each user, a name, a unique email address, a password (held
342	  securely — never retrievable or displayable in plain text), and exactly one role of `SUPPORT`,
343	  `GENERAL`, or `ADMIN`.
344	- **FR-003**: System MUST reject a login attempt with an incorrect password or an unregistered
345	  email using the same generic invalid-credentials error, and MUST NOT establish an authenticated
346	  context for a rejected attempt.
347	- **FR-004**: System MUST reject a login request missing the email or password field with a
348	  descriptive validation error.
349	- **FR-005**: System MUST be able to hold user account records (name, email, password, role) that
350	  exist prior to any login attempt; how those accounts are created or onboarded is out of scope
351	  for this feature (see Assumptions).
352	- **FR-006**: System MUST reject every request to this feature's APIs from a caller without an
353	  authenticated context, with the single exception of the login request itself (FR-001) — this
354	  includes, at minimum, ticket creation, ticket retrieval (single and list), ticket updates and
355	  status transitions, ticket reassignment, comment creation and retrieval, and chatbot queries.
356	  No API this feature exposes is reachable by an unauthenticated caller other than login.
357	- **FR-007**: System MUST reject a chatbot query request from a caller without an authenticated
358	  context, and MUST NOT generate a response (a specific instance of FR-006).
359	- **FR-008**: System MUST allow a logged-in user to explicitly log out, ending their
360	  authenticated context so that subsequent requests from them are treated as unauthenticated
361	  until they log in again.
362	
363	**Ticket assignment**
364	
365	- **FR-009**: System MUST NOT accept a caller-supplied assignee on ticket creation; the assignee
366	  MUST always be the system's own automatic choice.
367	- **FR-010**: Upon creating a ticket, system MUST automatically assign it to the `SUPPORT`-role
368	  user with the fewest tickets currently assigned to them in `OPEN` or `IN_PROGRESS` status (a
369	  ticket in `RESOLVED`, `CLOSED`, or `CANCELLED` status does not count toward their workload).
370	- **FR-011**: When two or more `SUPPORT` users are tied for the fewest counted tickets, system
371	  MUST select exactly one of them using a consistent, repeatable rule (e.g. a stable ordering),
372	  not an arbitrary or random choice.
373	- **FR-012**: When no `SUPPORT`-role user exists at ticket-creation time, system MUST still
374	  create the ticket, leaving it unassigned, rather than rejecting the creation request.
375	- **FR-013**: System MUST allow a user with the `ADMIN` role to manually reassign a ticket to a
376	  different `SUPPORT`-role user after its automatic assignment; no other role MAY manually
377	  reassign a ticket.
378	
379	**Comments**
380	
381	- **FR-014**: System MUST allow a comment to be added to a ticket only by the user who created
382	  that ticket or the user currently assigned to it, and MUST reject the request from any other
383	  user with a clear authorization error.
384	- **FR-015**: System MUST record, for every comment, the identity of the user who created it, and
385	  MUST return that user's name whenever the comment is displayed.
386	
387	**Ticket listing**
388	
389	- **FR-016**: System MUST allow a ticket-list request to be scoped to exactly one of: tickets
390	  created by the requesting user, tickets assigned to the requesting user, or all tickets the
391	  requesting user is permitted to see.
392	- **FR-017**: System MUST allow an ownership scope (FR-016) to be combined with the existing
393	  keyword and status filters, returning only tickets matching all supplied conditions together.
394	
395	**Chatbot knowledge base**
396	
397	- **FR-018**: System MUST automatically add a ticket's title, description, and comments to a
398	  knowledge base when the ticket reaches a resolved state, with no manual step required.
399	- **FR-019**: System MUST represent each knowledge base entry so that it can be retrieved by
400	  semantic similarity to a free-text query, not only exact keyword matches.
401	- **FR-020**: System MUST retain, per knowledge base entry, enough of the originating ticket's
402	  comments to identify what resolution was actually used.
403	
404	**Chatbot query & response**
405	
406	- **FR-021**: System MUST provide a chatbot interface that accepts a free-text query describing a
407	  user's issue.
408	- **FR-022**: System MUST reject empty or blank chatbot queries with a descriptive validation
409	  error, without invoking retrieval or the language model.
410	- **FR-023**: For each valid query, system MUST retrieve the past resolved ticket(s) most similar
411	  in meaning to the query.
412	- **FR-024**: System MUST generate the chatbot's response using the retrieved ticket(s)'
413	  comments/resolution content as grounding, so the answer reflects a real historical resolution.
414	- **FR-025**: System MUST identify, alongside each chatbot response, which past ticket(s) the
415	  response was grounded in, using a reference that does not itself expose internal-only ticket
416	  data (e.g. a ticket reference number, not a raw internal record dump).
417	- **FR-026**: System MUST NOT use a ticket that is not in a resolved state as grounding for a
418	  chatbot response.
419	- **FR-027**: System MUST NOT present a knowledge base entry with no resolution content
420	  (title/description only, no comments) as the basis for a resolution.
421	- **FR-028**: When no past resolved ticket is a sufficiently close match to the query, system
422	  MUST tell the user no confident match was found instead of fabricating a resolution, and MUST
423	  direct the user to raise a ticket manually through the existing ticket-creation flow. The
424	  chatbot MUST NOT create a ticket automatically on the user's behalf.
425	- **FR-029**: System MUST keep the knowledge base consistent with the resolved-ticket data it was
426	  built from — a concurrent chatbot query MUST be served against a coherent knowledge base state,
427	  never a partially updated one.
428	- **FR-030**: System MUST return a clear, distinct error when knowledge base retrieval or
429	  response generation is unavailable, rather than an empty or silently incorrect answer.
430	
431	**Chatbot customer-safety**
432	
433	- **FR-031**: System MUST NOT surface internal-only ticket or comment content verbatim in a
434	  chatbot response; the resolution content from matched tickets MUST be reworded into a
435	  customer-appropriate answer before being returned.
436	- **FR-032**: System MUST NOT expose, in a chatbot response, any identifying details of the
437	  customer(s) or agent(s) associated with the matched past ticket(s) (e.g. names, contact
438	  information, internal assignee identifiers).
439	
440	**Chatbot conversation**
441	
442	- **FR-033**: System MUST maintain conversation context across multiple turns within the same
443	  chatbot conversation, so a follow-up query is interpreted in light of earlier turns rather than
444	  in isolation.
445	- **FR-034**: System MUST use the ongoing conversation's context, in addition to the current
446	  query, when retrieving and grounding a follow-up response.
447	- **FR-035**: System MUST retain a chatbot conversation (its queries and responses) for 90 days
448	  after the conversation ends, then delete it.
449	- **FR-036**: System MUST end a chatbot conversation when the user explicitly ends it, or after
450	  30 minutes with no new query in that conversation, whichever occurs first.
451	
452	### Key Entities
453	
454	- **User**: A person who can log in. Attributes: unique identifier, name, unique email, securely
455	  held password, role (`SUPPORT`, `GENERAL`, or `ADMIN`).
456	- **Ticket** *(extends the existing Ticket entity)*: Its assignee is now a reference to a
457	  `SUPPORT`-role `User` chosen automatically by the system, rather than free-form text supplied by
458	  a caller, and it additionally carries a reference to the `User` who created it.
459	- **Comment** *(extends the existing Comment entity)*: Now carries a reference to the `User` who
460	  created it, and that user's name is what is shown as the comment's creator.
461	- **Knowledge Base Entry**: A retrievable representation of one resolved ticket's title and
462	  description, used to find matches for a chatbot query. Carries a reference back to its source
463	  ticket and the resolution content (comments) needed to ground an answer.
464	- **Chatbot Conversation**: An ongoing exchange between one logged-in `User` and the chatbot,
465	  spanning one or more turns. Attributes: unique identifier, the `User` who owns it, start
466	  timestamp, ordered sequence of queries and responses that make up its turns, retained for 90
467	  days after the conversation ends then deleted.
468	- **Chatbot Query**: A free-text question or issue description submitted by a user as one turn of
469	  a conversation. Attributes: the query text, timestamp, the response ultimately produced for it,
470	  and a reference to its parent conversation.
471	- **Chatbot Response**: The answer returned to a chatbot query. Attributes: response text, the
472	  set of source ticket(s) it was grounded in (or an explicit no-match indicator), timestamp.
473	
474	## Success Criteria *(mandatory)*
475	
476	### Measurable Outcomes
477	
478	- **SC-001**: 100% of attempts to call any API this feature exposes — other than login itself —
479	  made without being logged in, are rejected, verified across the full automated test suite.
480	- **SC-002**: 100% of newly created tickets are assigned to the `SUPPORT` user who, at the moment
481	  of creation, has the fewest counted tickets — verified by automated tests covering ties and
482	  varying load distributions.
483	- **SC-003**: 100% of comment attempts by a user who is neither a ticket's creator nor its
484	  assignee are rejected, and 100% of comments by a user who is either are accepted and correctly
485	  attributed by name.
486	- **SC-004**: Users can retrieve a ticket list scoped to "created by me," "assigned to me," or
487	  "all," and each scope returns exactly the expected subset in 100% of test cases, including when
488	  combined with an existing keyword or status filter.
489	- **SC-005**: No password is ever observable in plain text in any API response, log, or stored
490	  record, verified by review of every response and log format the feature introduces.
491	- **SC-006**: For a query closely matching an existing resolved ticket's issue, the chatbot
492	  returns a response grounded in that ticket's actual resolution in at least 90% of such queries
493	  during testing.
494	- **SC-007**: A newly resolved ticket becomes usable as grounding for a matching chatbot query
495	  without any manual re-indexing step, verified for 100% of tickets resolved during testing.
496	- **SC-008**: When no sufficiently similar past ticket exists, the chatbot states it has no
497	  confident match rather than fabricating one, in 100% of such cases during testing.
498	- **SC-009**: Users can receive a chatbot response, including which past ticket(s) grounded it,
499	  in under 5 seconds under normal load, defined as a knowledge base of up to 50,000 resolved
500	  tickets and up to 100 concurrent chatbot conversations.
501	- **SC-010**: 100% of chatbot responses grounded in past tickets identify the specific ticket(s)
502	  used, so a user can verify the source.
503	
504	## Assumptions
505	
506	- This feature amends 001/002's original assumptions where they conflict: ticket assignment
507	  (previously a free-form value the caller could set — spec 001, FR-001/FR-004) is now
508	  exclusively automatic and role-constrained; comment authorship (previously "no separate
509	  authenticated author field" — spec 002) now requires an authenticated creator whose name is
510	  recorded and shown.
511	- "All tickets the requesting user is permitted to see" (FR-016) defaults to every ticket for
512	  `SUPPORT` and `ADMIN` users, and to only the tickets a `GENERAL` user created for a `GENERAL`
513	  user — a `GENERAL` user cannot list tickets they did not create, since they are never an
514	  assignee.
515	- A default ticket-list request with no ownership scope specified (User Story 7, Scenario 3)
516	  applies that same permitted-visibility rule as its default, preserving the existing "list all"
517	  behavior for `SUPPORT`/`ADMIN` without exposing other users' tickets to `GENERAL` users.
518	- Password storage and transmission follow standard secure-credential practice (one-way hashing
519	  at rest, never logged or returned); the specific mechanism is a planning decision, not a scope
520	  decision.
521	- An authenticated session/context, once established by login, is assumed to apply to a caller's
522	  subsequent requests for a reasonable duration; specific session lifetime/expiry is a planning
523	  decision not addressed by this spec.
524	- User account creation/onboarding (who can create an account, and who may set a `SUPPORT` or
525	  `ADMIN` role) is explicitly out of scope for this feature and will be decided in a later
526	  feature. For this feature, user accounts (including `SUPPORT` and `ADMIN` users) are assumed to
527	  already exist as seed data populated at deployment time.
528	- Login brute-force/lockout protection and chatbot query rate-limiting/abuse protection are both
529	  out of scope for this feature, deferred to the infrastructure/gateway layer.
530	- Password strength/complexity rules are out of scope for this feature, since user account
531	  creation/update is out of scope (FR-005); any such rule belongs to the future account-creation
532	  feature.
533	- "Resolved state" for knowledge-base inclusion means the ticket has reached `RESOLVED` (or later
534	  `CLOSED`) per the existing ticket lifecycle; tickets in `OPEN`, `IN_PROGRESS`, or `CANCELLED`
535	  are never used as grounding.
536	- The knowledge base is derived data built from existing ticket/comment records; it does not
537	  introduce a new source of truth for ticket content — the ticket and its comments remain
538	  authoritative.
539	- One resolved ticket can produce at most one knowledge base entry, refreshed if its comments
540	  change after resolution (e.g. a late clarifying comment), rather than one entry per comment.
541	- "User" throughout the chatbot-related requirements means any logged-in user regardless of role
542	  (`GENERAL`, `SUPPORT`, or `ADMIN`) — the chatbot is not restricted to one role, mirroring how
543	  ticket creation is open to every logged-in role.
544	- Reworded/customer-safe chatbot response content (FR-031) means the resolution steps are
545	  conveyed without exposing raw internal comment text, internal notes, or people's identifying
546	  details (FR-032) — the specific rewording mechanism is a planning decision, not a scope
547	  decision.
548	- FR-006's "only login is open" boundary applies to this feature's business APIs (tickets,
549	  comments, chatbot). It deliberately does not extend to operational/infrastructure endpoints
550	  (health checks, API documentation) — those are outside this feature's scope and already
551	  governed separately by the project constitution.
552	- This amendment closes a gap the original merge left implicit: ticket/comment retrieval and
553	  listing were not previously named as requiring login, and — because this feature's ticket/
554	  comment responses now carry real user names (`createdBy`, `assignee`, comment author) — leaving
555	  them open would have exposed that identifying information to anonymous callers. FR-006 now
556	  closes that gap explicitly rather than leaving it to be decided during planning.
557
```

Scan against the widened FR-006 surfaces one real gap. Asking it now.

**Question:** Can a `GENERAL` user view a single ticket (or its comments) by ID that they neither created nor are assigned to?

Why it matters: FR-006 now only checks "is the caller logged in," not "is this their ticket" — tickets carry real names and comment content, so an open single-ticket view would let any customer see another customer's ticket just by knowing/guessing its ID.

**Recommended:** Option A - matches the visibility rule this spec already established for listing ("a `GENERAL` user cannot list tickets they did not create") — extending the same rule to single-ticket/comment view is the consistent default and closes an otherwise-real privacy gap.

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| A | Restrict single-ticket/comment view to the ticket's creator, its assignee, or a `SUPPORT`/`ADMIN` user — same visibility rule as listing's "all" scope |
| B | Any logged-in user can view any ticket by ID — login is the only gate, no ownership check |
| Short | Provide a different short answer (≤5 words) |

You can reply with the option letter (e.g., "A"), accept the recommendation by saying "yes" or "recommended", or provide your own short answer.

````markdown
# Implementation Plan: Authenticated Ticketing with RAG Resolution Chatbot

**Branch**: `005-auth-rag-chatbot` | **Date**: 2026-09-22 | **Spec**: [spec.md](./spec.md)

**Input**: Feature specification from `/specs/005-auth-rag-chatbot/spec.md`

## Summary

Add email/password login (`SUPPORT`/`GENERAL`/`ADMIN` roles) and make it the single gate in
front of every API this service exposes except login itself (FR-006, widened by this spec's
2026-09-22 amendment) — including, newly, single-ticket/comment view, which additionally gets a
row-level ownership check (FR-037: creator, assignee, or `SUPPORT`/`ADMIN`). On top of that
authenticated foundation: auto-assign each new ticket to the least-loaded `SUPPORT` user with
`ADMIN`-only manual override; restrict commenting to a ticket's creator or assignee with named
attribution; add ownership-scoped ticket listing; and build the RAG chatbot — a knowledge base of
resolved tickets, embedded and stored in the existing PostgreSQL database via the `pgvector`
extension (no new service), semantically retrieved per query, and answered by an LLM call that
grounds its response in the matched ticket(s)' actual resolution while staying customer-safe
(FR-031/032) — with multi-turn conversation support, a 90-day retention window, and a 30-minute
inactivity boundary. This is a single plan for a single merged spec (005), replacing two earlier,
disconnected efforts: 003 (chatbot) was never planned, and 004 (auth) was planned in isolation
against a chatbot endpoint that didn't exist — both spec.md files carry a superseded notice
pointing here.

## Technical Context

**Language/Version**: Java 25 (LTS) — unchanged, constitution-fixed.

**Primary Dependencies**: Spring Boot 3.5.16 (Spring Web, Spring Data JPA, Spring Validation,
Actuator) — already present. Adds `spring-boot-starter-security` (session-based authentication,
`BCryptPasswordEncoder`) and `spring-security-test` (test scope). Adds `pgvector` (the
`com.pgvector:pgvector` Java library — a small Hibernate/JDBC type mapper, not a database
driver) so a `Ticket`-derived embedding can be stored as a native PostgreSQL `vector` column
through JPA like any other field. No vector-database client library, no message broker, no LLM
SDK — the two external AI calls (embeddings, response generation) are plain HTTPS JSON calls made
through Spring's existing `RestClient` (already available via `spring-boot-starter-web`), wrapped
behind two small interfaces (`EmbeddingClient`, `ResolutionLlmClient`) so tests substitute a
deterministic stub instead of calling a real third-party API.

**Storage**: PostgreSQL 16+. The `vector` extension (via `pgvector`) is enabled on the same
database — no separate vector database service. New tables: `users`; `knowledge_base_entries`
(one row per resolved ticket, carrying its embedding); `chatbot_conversations`; `chatbot_turns`
(query + response per turn). `tickets` gains `created_by_id`/`assignee_id` (replacing the old
free-text `assignee`); `comments` gains `author_id`. All additive, forward-only Flyway migrations
(`V3`–`V9`).

**Testing**: JUnit 5, Spring Boot Test, Testcontainers (PostgreSQL — including a `pgvector/pgvector`
Testcontainers image so the vector column and similarity queries are tested against the real
extension, not skipped), AssertJ, `spring-security-test`. `EmbeddingClient`/`ResolutionLlmClient`
are swapped for a fixed-response test double in `@SpringBootTest` configuration — no test ever
calls a real external AI API (nondeterministic, costly, and not what Testcontainers' "real
PostgreSQL" mandate is about — that mandate is specifically for *persistence*, not third-party
network calls).

**Target Platform**: Same single Spring Boot microservice; no new deployable, no new service.

**Project Type**: Backend extension to an existing web-service. No frontend work in scope.

**Performance Goals**: Chatbot response (retrieval + generation) under 5 seconds under normal
load — up to 50,000 resolved tickets in the knowledge base, up to 100 concurrent conversations
(SC-009). Existing 2-second ticket-search/comment-list targets (001/002) unchanged. 50,000 vectors
is comfortably within `pgvector`'s HNSW-index range for sub-second similarity search, so response
time is dominated by the external LLM call, not retrieval.

**Constraints**: Reuses constitution-mandated patterns: contract-first (OpenAPI before controller
code), constructor injection only, single local `@Transactional` per unit of work (no SAGA — every
call in this feature, including the AI calls, stays inside this service's own request; there is
no cross-*service* call, since the AI providers are external APIs consumed synchronously, the
same category as any other outbound HTTP call this codebase already makes to nothing today but
would to Flyway/Postgres-adjacent tooling), paginated list endpoints, one consistent `ApiError`
shape, structured logging with correlation IDs. This plan additionally closes a gap the prior
(now-superseded) 004 plan left open: `TicketService`'s transition log line never included the
acting user, even though constitution Principle V requires it — `CurrentUser` (this feature's own
addition) makes that fixable, and it is fixed here (see research.md).

**Scale/Scope**: Two new controllers (`AuthController`, `ChatbotController`), five new domain
packages (`user`, `auth`, `knowledgebase`, `chatbot`, `ai`), seven additive migrations, and
modifications to every existing ticket/comment code path (create, view, list, update, transition,
comment) to add authentication, ownership authorization, and named attribution. User account
creation itself stays out of scope (spec FR-005) — accounts are seed data.

## Constitution Check

*GATE: Must pass before Phase 0 research. Re-check after Phase 1 design.*

| Principle / Rule | Status | How this plan satisfies it |
|---|---|---|
| I. Contract-First API Design | PASS | `contracts/auth-api.yaml`, `contracts/ticket-ownership-api.yaml`, and `contracts/chatbot-api.yaml` are written before controller code. All endpoints stay under `/api/v1/...`. No entity (`User` least of all — its password field) is ever serialized directly. |
| II. Domain Invariants Enforced in the Backend | PASS | Comment authorization (creator-or-assignee), single-ticket/comment view authorization (FR-037: creator/assignee/`SUPPORT`/`ADMIN`), and reassignment authorization (`ADMIN`-only) are data-dependent rules enforced in `TicketService`/`CommentService`, not the controller or client. The ticket status state machine itself is untouched. |
| III. Test-First, State Machine Covered | PASS | Contract and integration tests for login/logout, the now-blanket authentication gate (including the two view endpoints that were previously open), auto-assignment, `ADMIN`-only reassignment, comment authorization, listing scope, knowledge-base indexing, chatbot retrieval/grounding/no-match/conversation behavior, and retention cleanup are written before their implementations. |
| IV. PostgreSQL as the Single Source of Truth | PASS | Seven additive, forward-only Flyway migrations (`V3`–`V9`); `ddl-auto` stays `validate`; every new relationship gets a foreign key; every new lookup path gets an index (assignment workload, ownership scope, vector similarity via an HNSW index). The knowledge base's vectors live in this same PostgreSQL database via `pgvector` — no second datastore, so this feature introduces no new "source of truth" to reconcile. |
| V. Observability, Secrets Hygiene, Simplicity | PASS | Every login attempt, auto-assignment decision, and now every ticket status transition (including its actor — the gap the prior plan left open) is logged with the existing correlation ID. No password is ever logged/returned/stored in plain text. The two new external calls are the only new "service-like" dependency, and they are unavoidable (an LLM has to run *somewhere*) rather than optional infrastructure; `pgvector` was chosen specifically *to avoid* adding a vector-database service, per this principle's "no unjustified complexity" — the named concrete problem (semantic retrieval at ≤50k rows) does not require one. |
| Design Patterns: constructor injection | PASS | Every new class (`AuthController`, `ChatbotController`, `EmbeddingClient`/`ResolutionLlmClient` implementations, services) takes dependencies via constructor. |
| Design Patterns: atomicity / SAGA scope | PASS | Ticket creation (including auto-assignment) stays one local `@Transactional` unit of work. Knowledge-base indexing runs *after* the resolving transaction commits (`@TransactionalEventListener(AFTER_COMMIT)` + `@Async`), so a slow or failed embedding call can never roll back or block the ticket transition itself — deliberately decoupled, not a SAGA (no compensating action is needed; a missed index entry is simply picked up by the next resolution event, and is not a correctness failure of the ticket record). |

No violations. Complexity Tracking is empty — the one new "service-like" dependency
(`pgvector`, not a new service) is justified above.
````

```markdown
# Phase 0 Research: Authenticated Ticketing with RAG Resolution Chatbot

Technical Context has no unresolved `NEEDS CLARIFICATION` — the constitution and 001/002's own
research already fix the base stack. This research covers two groups of decisions: the
authentication/authorization layer (carried over from the now-superseded 004 plan, still valid
against this merged spec, updated for the widened FR-006/new FR-037), and the RAG chatbot itself
(new — 003 was never planned).

## Part A — Authentication & Access Control

### Authentication mechanism

- **Decision**: `spring-boot-starter-security`, with a custom `POST /api/v1/auth/login` JSON
  endpoint that authenticates via `AuthenticationManager` and saves the resulting
  `SecurityContext` into the servlet `HttpSession`, plus `POST /api/v1/auth/logout` to invalidate
  it. Passwords hashed with `BCryptPasswordEncoder`.
- **Rationale**: One dependency already in the Spring Boot BOM satisfies FR-001–004/008. Nothing
  in the spec calls for statelessness, mobile clients, or third-party identity federation.
- **Alternatives considered**: JWT — rejected, solves a horizontal-scalability problem the spec
  never raises. OAuth2/OIDC — rejected; the constitution previously removed its OAuth2 rule by
  explicit amendment.

### Session storage

- **Decision**: The default in-process servlet `HttpSession`.
- **Rationale**: Simplest option; session lifetime/expiry is explicitly a planning decision per
  spec.md Assumptions, and nothing in scope requires more than the single deployable this already
  is.
- **Alternatives considered**: Spring Session/JDBC — rejected for now; the correct upgrade only
  if/when this service is horizontally scaled, which no requirement establishes today.

### Endpoint access rules (updated for the widened FR-006)

- **Decision**: `SecurityConfig` is now genuinely default-deny: `permitAll` on `POST
  /api/v1/auth/login` and the operational endpoints outside this feature's scope (`GET
  /actuator/health`, `GET /actuator/info`, `/v3/api-docs/**`, `/swagger-ui/**`); `anyRequest()
  .authenticated()` for everything else — ticket creation, view, list, update, transition,
  reassignment, comment creation and retrieval, and every chatbot endpoint.
- **Rationale**: FR-006 (as amended 2026-09-22) states this directly: "No API this feature
  exposes is reachable by an unauthenticated caller other than login." This removes the
  now-superseded 004 plan's special-cased `permitAll` for `GET /tickets/{id}` and `GET
  /tickets/{id}/comments` — those two endpoints are no longer exceptions.
- **Alternatives considered**: An explicit allow-list naming only the endpoints spec FRs mention
  by name — rejected; FR-006's own wording is the blanket rule, not a per-endpoint enumeration,
  and a narrower matcher would silently miss future endpoints (exactly the gap the amendment was
  written to close).

### View authorization (NEW — FR-037)

- **Decision**: Authentication (via `SecurityConfig`) answers "is there a caller"; a separate,
  data-dependent check in `TicketService.getById`/`getDetailById` (and the comment-list path,
  which loads the parent ticket first) answers "may *this* caller see *this* ticket" — allowed
  when the caller is the ticket's `createdById`, its `assigneeId`, or has role `SUPPORT`/`ADMIN`;
  otherwise a `ForbiddenActionException` (403).
- **Rationale**: Constitution Principle II: business rules a route matcher can't express (which
  specific ticket, which specific caller) belong in the domain layer. Exactly the same pattern
  already used for comment-creation authorization (FR-014) and reassignment authorization
  (FR-013).
- **Alternatives considered**: Restricting `SUPPORT` to only tickets assigned to them (not
  blanket view) — rejected; spec.md's Assumptions already establish `SUPPORT`/`ADMIN` see "every
  ticket" for *listing* (FR-016's "all" scope), so restricting single-ticket *view* more tightly
  than listing would be an inconsistent, unrequested rule.

### Authorization model (general)

- **Decision**: Purely role-based checks (e.g. "must be `ADMIN`" for reassignment) are Spring
  Security matcher/`@PreAuthorize` rules. Checks that depend on *which* ticket is involved
  (comment authorship, view authorization) are enforced in `TicketService`/`CommentService`.
- **Rationale**: Same constitution Principle II reasoning as above.

### Data model: assignee and comment authorship become real identities

- **Decision**: `tickets.assignee` (free-text) is replaced with `assignee_id` (nullable UUID FK
  to `users`); `tickets` gains `created_by_id` (UUID FK, not null); `comments` gains `author_id`
  (UUID FK, not null).
- **Rationale**: Constitution Principle IV ("foreign keys on all relationships"); the only way to
  enforce FR-009/FR-010 (assignee must be a real `SUPPORT` user) and FR-014/FR-015 (comment
  authorship must be a real, named user) at the database level.
- **Migration note**: Both new not-null foreign keys are added directly as `NOT NULL` — this
  codebase has no ticket/comment data predating this feature in any environment the migration
  runs against (only 001/002 have shipped; confirmed no `User`/auth code exists yet).

### Auto-assignment algorithm

- **Decision**: `UserRepository` exposes a query: among `role = 'SUPPORT'` users, count each
  one's tickets where `assignee_id = user.id AND status IN ('OPEN','IN_PROGRESS')`, order by that
  count ascending then `id` ascending, take the first row. Same query backs
  `TicketService.create()`'s assignment step inside the ticket's own `@Transactional` block.
- **Rationale**: Directly implements FR-010 (workload = `OPEN`+`IN_PROGRESS`) and FR-011
  (tie-break by stable, deterministic order). A composite index on `tickets (assignee_id,
  status)` keeps the aggregate cheap.
- **Concurrency trade-off**: Two tickets created in true-concurrent transactions could both read
  the same "least-loaded" user before either commits. Accepted as a soft heuristic, not a
  correctness invariant — SC-002 is verified by sequential test scenarios. Adding row-level
  locking for this is unjustified complexity per constitution Principle V.

### Manual reassignment

- **Decision**: A dedicated `PATCH /api/v1/tickets/{ticketId}/assignee`, `ADMIN`-only, taking
  `{ assigneeId }`. The general `PATCH /api/v1/tickets/{ticketId}` body no longer accepts
  `assignee` at all.
- **Rationale**: FR-013 makes `ADMIN` reassignment the *only* legal way to change an assignee
  after creation; keeping it in the general update DTO would let any ticket-updater silently
  change the assignee too.

### Listing scope semantics

- **Decision**: `GET /api/v1/tickets` gains `scope` (`mine`, `assigned`, `all`; default `all`).
  `all` always means "every ticket the caller is permitted to see" — for `SUPPORT`/`ADMIN` that's
  every ticket; for `GENERAL` it narrows to tickets they created. `assigned` for a `GENERAL`
  caller returns an empty page, not an error.
- **Rationale**: Matches FR-016 and spec.md Assumptions exactly.

### Seed users

- **Decision**: Demo/seed `User` rows (one `ADMIN`, two `SUPPORT`, one `GENERAL`) via a
  `@Profile("dev")` `CommandLineRunner`, never a Flyway migration.
- **Rationale**: Constitution Principle V forbids committing a credential "in any form... test
  fixtures... example config" — a Flyway migration runs identically in every environment,
  including a future production one; a dev-only seeder never executes there.

### CORS and CSRF

- **Decision**: `CorsConfig` → `allowCredentials(true)` (required for the session cookie
  cross-origin); origins stay an explicit allow-list. CSRF disabled — this is a JSON-only API
  with no server-rendered forms; the session cookie's `SameSite` attribute plus the strict CORS
  allow-list mitigate.

### Fixing the actor-logging gap (constitution Principle V)

- **Decision**: `TicketService.applyTransition`'s existing log line
  (`ticket_transition ticketId={} from={} to={}`) gains a fourth field, `actor={}`, populated
  from `CurrentUser`.
- **Rationale**: Constitution Principle V states plainly: "Every ticket state transition MUST be
  logged with ticket identifier, previous status, new status, **and actor**." This was
  unsatisfiable before any authentication existed (001/002 predate it); this feature is what
  makes an actor identity available, so this plan closes the gap rather than carrying it forward
  a third time.

## Part B — RAG Resolution Chatbot

### Vector storage: `pgvector` on the existing PostgreSQL vs. a dedicated vector database

- **Decision**: Enable the `vector` extension on the existing PostgreSQL instance (via the
  `pgvector` Postgres extension and the small `com.pgvector:pgvector` Java type-mapping library),
  and store each `KnowledgeBaseEntry`'s embedding as a native `vector` column with an HNSW index.
- **Rationale**: Constitution Principle IV names PostgreSQL as *the* single source of truth, and
  Principle V forbids a new service without a named, concrete problem it solves. At the spec's
  own stated scale (SC-009: up to 50,000 resolved tickets), `pgvector`'s HNSW index delivers
  sub-second approximate nearest-neighbor search — there is no concrete problem (throughput,
  latency, dataset size) that a dedicated vector database would solve here that `pgvector`
  doesn't already. It also means the knowledge base is backed up, migrated, and transactionally
  consistent with the ticket data it's derived from, using the exact same operational tooling
  (Flyway, `pg_dump`, Testcontainers) the rest of the service already relies on.
- **Alternatives considered**: A standalone vector database (Pinecone, Weaviate, Qdrant, etc.) —
  rejected; would be a new external service requiring its own availability story, its own backup/
  DR story, and its own dependency-vulnerability surface, all to solve a scale problem (50k
  vectors) `pgvector` already solves inside the existing database.

### Embedding generation

- **Decision**: Call an external embedding API over plain HTTPS (via Spring's `RestClient`,
  already available) from `HttpEmbeddingClient`, an implementation of the `EmbeddingClient`
  interface. Concretely: Voyage AI's embeddings endpoint — Anthropic's own recommended embeddings
  partner (Anthropic does not offer a first-party embeddings API), avoiding a third,
  unrelated AI vendor in the stack.
- **Rationale**: FR-019 requires semantic retrievability; an embedding model is the standard way
  to get there, and this keeps the AI vendor surface to two related providers instead of three
  unrelated ones.
- **Alternatives considered**: A locally-hosted open-source embedding model — rejected; adds a
  model-serving component (GPU/CPU capacity planning, model file management) that is exactly the
  kind of new-service complexity Principle V asks to avoid when an equivalent hosted API already
  satisfies the requirement at this scale.

### Response generation (the LLM call)

- **Decision**: Call Anthropic's Claude Messages API over plain HTTPS from
  `HttpResolutionLlmClient`, an implementation of `ResolutionLlmClient`. The system prompt
  constrains the model to: (a) answer only from the matched ticket(s)' comments/resolution
  content passed in as context, (b) never quote internal comment text verbatim — rephrase it
  (FR-031), (c) never include a customer's or agent's name, contact info, or internal identifier
  (FR-032), (d) explicitly say so when asked to answer outside the provided context (keeps FR-028
  strict — the model doesn't get to freelance a "confident match" the retrieval step didn't find).
- **Rationale**: FR-024 requires the response be LLM-grounded on retrieved content, not merely
  keyword-stitched. A single HTTPS call, no SDK, matches the same "small, testable client
  interface" pattern as the embedding client.
- **Alternatives considered**: A self-hosted open-source LLM — rejected for the same
  capacity-planning/Principle-V reason as the embedding alternative, and quality of grounded,
  customer-safe rewording (FR-031) is materially harder to guarantee from a smaller local model.

### Knowledge base indexing trigger

- **Decision**: `TicketService.applyTransition` publishes a `TicketResolvedEvent` (Spring
  `ApplicationEventPublisher`) when a ticket reaches `RESOLVED`. `KnowledgeBaseService` listens
  via `@TransactionalEventListener(phase = AFTER_COMMIT)` and, in a separate `@Async` method,
  calls `EmbeddingClient`, builds/refreshes the `KnowledgeBaseEntry`, and saves it in its own
  transaction.
- **Rationale**: FR-018 requires no manual step, but nothing in the spec requires the embedding
  call to complete before the ticket-transition HTTP response returns — decoupling it keeps a
  slow or briefly-failing embedding call from ever affecting the ticket transition's own latency
  or correctness. `AFTER_COMMIT` guarantees the source ticket's `RESOLVED` state is durable before
  indexing reads it.
- **Alternatives considered**: Synchronous indexing inside the same `@Transactional` block —
  rejected; holds a database connection open for the duration of an external HTTP call, and a
  transient embedding-API failure would then fail the ticket transition itself, which FR-018
  does not require and which would be a worse user experience for no benefit.

### Retrieval & grounding

- **Decision**: `ChatbotService` embeds the incoming query (same `EmbeddingClient`), runs a
  `pgvector` cosine-distance `ORDER BY ... LIMIT k` query via `KnowledgeBaseEntryRepository`
  filtered to entries with non-empty resolution content (FR-027), and treats a result "confident"
  only if its similarity clears a configurable threshold (`ChatbotProperties.similarityThreshold`,
  a conservative default, tunable without a code change). Below threshold → FR-028's no-match
  path, no LLM call made (saves cost, keeps the "honest" behavior server-side rather than
  hoping the prompt enforces it).
- **Rationale**: FR-023, FR-026, FR-027, FR-028 combined. Deciding "confident vs. not" before
  ever calling the LLM is simpler and cheaper than asking the LLM to self-report low confidence.
- **Alternatives considered**: Always calling the LLM and asking it to say "I don't know" when
  the context is weak — rejected; less reliable (an LLM can still fabricate) and strictly more
  expensive (an unnecessary generation call) than a numeric threshold check the code already has
  to compute anyway for ranking.

### Conversation model & the 30-minute inactivity boundary

- **Decision**: A `ChatbotConversation` has `startedAt` and (via its turns) an implicit
  `lastActivityAt`. On each incoming query, `ChatbotService` looks for the caller's open
  conversation (no explicit end, last turn within 30 minutes); if none, it starts a new one. No
  background job marks a conversation "ended" — ending is computed at query time.
- **Rationale**: FR-036's "explicit end or 30-minute inactivity, whichever first" only needs to
  be evaluated when a new query arrives — computing it lazily avoids a second scheduled job on
  top of the retention cleanup, and matches "start with the simplest design."
- **Alternatives considered**: A `@Scheduled` sweep that actively flips conversations to "ended"
  after 30 minutes — rejected; the state of an idle conversation has no observable effect between
  queries, so proactively updating it accomplishes nothing a lazy check doesn't already achieve.

### 90-day conversation retention

- **Decision**: A daily `@Scheduled` `ConversationRetentionJob` deletes `ChatbotConversation`
  rows (cascading their turns) whose effective end time is more than 90 days in the past.
- **Rationale**: FR-035. Spring's built-in `@Scheduled` needs no new dependency or external
  scheduler.

### External-API failure handling

- **Decision**: Both AI clients wrap their HTTP call in a try/catch; any failure (timeout,
  non-2xx, malformed response) is translated to `AiServiceUnavailableException`, mapped to `503`
  with a distinct `ApiError` code (FR-030). One bounded retry (single retry, short timeout) is
  applied to the embedding call only (idempotent, cheap); the generation call is not retried
  automatically (an LLM call is comparatively expensive and a user-visible retry is preferable to
  a silent doubled-cost one).
- **Alternatives considered**: A circuit breaker (e.g. Resilience4j) — rejected as unjustified
  complexity per constitution Principle V; nothing in the spec's scale (100 concurrent
  conversations) demands it, and a single try/catch plus a clear error already satisfies FR-030.

### Testing the AI integration without calling real external APIs

- **Decision**: `EmbeddingClient`/`ResolutionLlmClient` are interfaces; production wiring injects
  the `Http*` implementations, but `@SpringBootTest` configurations for chatbot tests override
  those beans with fixed-response test doubles (deterministic embeddings for known fixture text;
  a canned grounded/no-match response).
- **Rationale**: Constitution Principle III's Testcontainers mandate is specifically about
  *persistence* tests against a real PostgreSQL — it says nothing about third-party network
  calls, which would make CI flaky, slow, and costly if left real. `pgvector` similarity search
  itself **is** tested against the real extension (via the `pgvector/pgvector` Testcontainers
  image), keeping the part this codebase owns fully real while stubbing the part it doesn't.

## Outcome

No unresolved `NEEDS CLARIFICATION` markers. Ready for Phase 1.

```

````markdown
# Phase 1 Data Model: Authenticated Ticketing with RAG Resolution Chatbot

## User (NEW)

| Field | Type | Rules |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | UUID (PK) | Generated at creation. |
| `name` | `VARCHAR(200)` | Not null. |
| `email` | `VARCHAR(320)` | Not null. Unique, case-insensitively (`LOWER(email)` unique index) — FR-002/FR-003. |
| `passwordHash` | `VARCHAR(200)` | Not null. `BCryptPasswordEncoder` output — never exposed by any DTO, never logged (FR-002, SC-005). |
| `role` | `UserRole` enum, string-stored | Not null. Exactly one of `SUPPORT`, `GENERAL`, `ADMIN` (FR-002). |
| `createdAt`/`updatedAt` | `TIMESTAMPTZ` | Set on persist/update. |

No lifecycle here — account creation is out of scope (FR-005); rows are seed data.

## Ticket (EXTENDS existing entity from 001)

| Field | Change |
|---|---|
| `assignee` (was free text) | **Replaced** by `assigneeId` — nullable UUID FK to `users.id`, restricted at the service layer to a `SUPPORT` user (FR-009/FR-010). Nullable per FR-012 (no `SUPPORT` user available). |
| `createdById` | **New** — UUID FK to `users.id`, not null. |
| All other fields | Unchanged from 001. |

**Rules added by this feature**:
- `assigneeId` never accepted from a client on create (FR-009) or general update (FR-013) — only
  set by auto-assignment or the dedicated `ADMIN`-only reassignment endpoint.
- Viewing a single ticket (and, transitively, its comments) is restricted to `createdById`,
  `assigneeId`, or a caller with role `SUPPORT`/`ADMIN` (FR-037) — enforced in `TicketService`,
  not expressible as a column constraint.

**New indexes**: `idx_tickets_assignee_id_status (assignee_id, status)` (auto-assignment
workload query, FR-010); `idx_tickets_created_by_id (created_by_id)` (`scope=mine` listing and
FR-037's creator check).

## Comment (EXTENDS existing entity from 001/002)

| Field | Change |
|---|---|
| `authorId` | **New** — UUID FK to `users.id`, not null. |

**Rule added**: a comment may only be created when `authorId` equals the parent ticket's
`createdById` OR `assigneeId` (FR-014) — enforced in `CommentService` against the ticket's
current state.

## Knowledge Base Entry (NEW)

One row per resolved ticket usable as chatbot grounding (spec Key Entities: Knowledge Base
Entry).

| Field | Type | Rules |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | UUID (PK) | Generated at creation. |
| `ticketId` | UUID | Not null, unique (one entry per ticket — "at most one knowledge base entry" per spec.md Assumptions). References `tickets.id`. |
| `embedding` | `vector(n)` (`pgvector`) | Not null. Generated from the ticket's title + description (FR-018/FR-019) via `EmbeddingClient`; dimension `n` fixed by the chosen embedding model. |
| `resolutionContent` | `TEXT` | The originating ticket's comment/resolution text retained for grounding (FR-020). Empty/absent when the ticket has no comments — such an entry is indexed (title/description still searchable) but MUST NOT be used as a resolution source (FR-027, Edge Cases). |
| `hasResolutionContent` | `BOOLEAN` | Derived flag backing the FR-027 exclusion filter without re-parsing `resolutionContent` on every query. |
| `createdAt`/`updatedAt` | `TIMESTAMPTZ` | `updatedAt` bumps when a late comment refreshes `resolutionContent` (spec.md Assumptions: "refreshed if its comments change after resolution"). |

**New index**: an HNSW index on `embedding` (cosine distance) backing FR-023's similarity
retrieval at the spec's stated scale (SC-009: ≤50,000 entries).

**Rule**: a row is only created/refreshed when the source ticket is in `RESOLVED` or `CLOSED`
status (FR-018, FR-026); a ticket that leaves a resolved state does not currently retract its
entry mid-flight (Edge Cases: reopening is not part of this feature's scope, per the existing
ticket lifecycle).

## Chatbot Conversation (NEW)

| Field | Type | Rules |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | UUID (PK) | Generated at creation. |
| `userId` | UUID | Not null. References `users.id` — the logged-in caller who owns it. |
| `startedAt` | `TIMESTAMPTZ` | Not null. |
| `explicitlyEndedAt` | `TIMESTAMPTZ`, nullable | Set when the user explicitly ends the conversation (FR-036). |

**Derived, not stored**: "is this conversation still open" = `explicitlyEndedAt IS NULL AND
(last turn's `createdAt`, or `startedAt` if no turns yet) is within 30 minutes of now`
(research.md "Conversation model"). A new query with no open conversation starts a new row.

**New index**: `(user_id, started_at)` to find a caller's most recent conversation quickly.

**Retention**: rows (cascading their turns) older than 90 days past their effective end are
deleted by `ConversationRetentionJob` (FR-035).

## Chatbot Turn (NEW — implements spec's "Chatbot Query"/"Chatbot Response")

One row per query+response pair within a conversation.

| Field | Type | Rules |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | UUID (PK) | Generated at creation. |
| `conversationId` | UUID | Not null. References `chatbot_conversations.id`. |
| `queryText` | `TEXT` | Not null, non-blank (FR-022). |
| `responseText` | `TEXT` | Not null — either a grounded resolution (FR-024) or the no-match message (FR-028). |
| `sourceTicketIds` | `UUID[]` | The knowledge base entries' source tickets the response was grounded in (FR-025); empty when the response is a no-match. |
| `createdAt` | `TIMESTAMPTZ` | Not null; also the conversation's "last activity" marker. |

## Relationships

```text
User (1) ──< assigneeId       ── Ticket
User (1) ──< createdById      ── Ticket
User (1) ──< authorId         ── Comment
User (1) ──< userId           ── Chatbot Conversation
Ticket (1) ──< ticketId       ── Comment                      (unchanged from 001)
Ticket (1) ──< ticketId (0..1)── Knowledge Base Entry
Chatbot Conversation (1) ──< conversationId ── Chatbot Turn
```

## Migrations (Flyway, additive/forward-only per constitution Principle IV)

- **`V3__create_users_table.sql`**: `users` table, case-insensitive unique index on `email`,
  index on `role`.
- **`V4__ticket_ownership_and_assignment.sql`**: `tickets.created_by_id` (`NOT NULL`, FK),
  `tickets.assignee_id` (nullable, FK); drops old `tickets.assignee` text column;
  `idx_tickets_assignee_id_status`, `idx_tickets_created_by_id`.
- **`V5__comment_author.sql`**: `comments.author_id` (`NOT NULL`, FK).
- **`V6__enable_pgvector.sql`**: `CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS vector;`
- **`V7__create_knowledge_base_entries.sql`**: `knowledge_base_entries` table (including the
  `vector` column) and its HNSW index.
- **`V8__create_chatbot_conversations.sql`**: `chatbot_conversations` table and its
  `(user_id, started_at)` index.
- **`V9__create_chatbot_turns.sql`**: `chatbot_turns` table, FK to `chatbot_conversations`,
  `ON DELETE CASCADE` (so retention cleanup deleting a conversation removes its turns in one
  statement).

Both new not-null foreign keys in `V4`/`V5` are added directly as `NOT NULL` — no ticket/comment
data predates this feature (confirmed: no `User`/auth code exists in the codebase yet).

````

```yaml
openapi: 3.0.3
info:
  title: Authentication API
  version: "1.0"
  description: >
    Session-based: a successful login establishes an HTTP session (cookie); logout invalidates it
    (FR-001, FR-003, FR-004, FR-008). Login is the ONLY endpoint in this feature not requiring an
    existing authenticated context (FR-006).
servers:
  - url: /api/v1

paths:
  /auth/login:
    post:
      summary: Log in with email and password (FR-001)
      operationId: login
      security: []
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema: { $ref: '#/components/schemas/LoginRequest' }
      responses:
        '200':
          description: Authenticated; a session cookie is set
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: { $ref: '#/components/schemas/LoginResponse' }
        '400':
          description: Missing email or password (FR-004)
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: { $ref: '#/components/schemas/ApiError' }
        '401':
          description: >
            Incorrect password or unregistered email — same generic error either way (FR-003)
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: { $ref: '#/components/schemas/ApiError' }

  /auth/logout:
    post:
      summary: Log out, ending the current session (FR-008)
      operationId: logout
      responses:
        '204':
          description: Session ended
        '401':
          description: No authenticated session to end
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: { $ref: '#/components/schemas/ApiError' }

components:
  schemas:
    LoginRequest:
      type: object
      required: [email, password]
      properties:
        email: { type: string, format: email }
        password: { type: string, format: password }

    LoginResponse:
      type: object
      properties:
        id: { type: string, format: uuid }
        name: { type: string }
        email: { type: string, format: email }
        role: { $ref: '#/components/schemas/UserRole' }

    UserRole:
      type: string
      enum: [SUPPORT, GENERAL, ADMIN]

    ApiError:
      type: object
      description: Same shape used by every endpoint in this service (constitution Principle I).
      properties:
        code: { type: string }
        message: { type: string }
        fieldErrors:
          type: array
          items:
            type: object
            properties:
              field: { type: string }
              message: { type: string }

```
